name: Peter

timeline.note: Birth year is estimated from his adult activity during Jesus' ministry (c. AD 27-30). The death date rests on early church tradition (Eusebius, Origen) placing his martyrdom in Rome under Nero, not on Scripture itself.

interpretive_note: Matthew 16:18 ('you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church') has been read differently across Christian traditions — some identify 'this rock' with Peter's confession of faith, others with Peter himself in a foundational role among the apostles, and Roman Catholic tradition builds a doctrine of papal succession from it. The text itself does not adjudicate between these readings.
source_summary: Galilean fisherman called as one of the twelve apostles, first to confess Jesus as the Christ, denied Jesus three times the night of His arrest, restored and recommissioned by the risen Christ, and became a leading voice of the early church at Pentecost and in opening the gospel to Gentiles.
family_friendly_summary: Peter was a fisherman who left his nets behind to follow Jesus and became one of His closest friends and apostles. Peter sometimes got things wonderfully right, like when he bravely said Jesus was the promised Messiah — but he also made big mistakes, like when he denied even knowing Jesus three times during Jesus' hardest hour. After Jesus rose from the dead, He lovingly forgave Peter and gave him an important job: taking care of His followers. Peter went on to boldly preach about Jesus and helped many people become believers, even reaching out to people who weren't Jewish, which was a big step for the early church. Peter's story shows that even after failing badly, God can forgive us completely and still use us for important things.
adult_story: Simon, a Galilean fisherman, was called by Jesus early in His ministry and given the name Peter ('rock'), with his brother Andrew (Matthew 4:18-20; John 1:40-42). He became the most prominent of the twelve apostles — often speaking first, often wrong first. He confessed Jesus as the Christ, the Son of the living God, and heard Jesus call him a rock on which He would build His church (Matthew 16:16-18); minutes later, rebuking Jesus for predicting His own death, Peter was called Satan for setting his mind on man's concerns, not God's (Matthew 16:21-23). Peter walked briefly on water toward Jesus before fear overtook him (Matthew 14:28-31), and at the Last Supper swore he would die before disowning Jesus, only to deny Him three times within hours, exactly as predicted (Matthew 26:33-35, 69-75). Scripture does not omit this collapse to protect Peter's reputation. After the resurrection, the risen Christ restored Peter personally, asking three times whether he loved Him — matching the three denials — and recommissioned him to feed and shepherd His sheep (John 21:15-19). At Pentecost, Peter preached the sermon behind three thousand conversions, and later a vision sent him to the Gentile centurion Cornelius, opening the church's mission beyond Jewish believers (Acts 2; 10). Even after this, Paul publicly opposed Peter at Antioch for withdrawing from table fellowship with Gentile believers under pressure, calling it hypocrisy (Galatians 2:11-14). Tradition, not Scripture, holds Peter was later martyred in Rome, crucified upside down at his own request (John 21:18-19).
